description:

## Summary

The four local applications (DE Explorer, Signature Scoring, Drug Perturbation, Genome Explorer) lose `deploy: false` in `apps.yml`. Each app's in-app Source link opened `posit-dev/lifescience-shiny-gallery`, which is private. It now opens the app's directory in this repository, the same address as the GitHub button on the tile. The four `manifest.json` files get the new checksum of `app.R`.

## Verification

After Barret's first publish of an app: write the printed `content_id` into its tile in `apps.yml`, and the matrix reports it as `DEPLOY`.

title: Give the gallery a favicon
description:
## Summary

The site served no favicon at all: no `rel="icon"` tag in the rendered page, and `/favicon.ico` answers 404 on the live site, so a browser tab showed the default blank icon.

`favicon.png` is the Shiny hex. It is the file `shiny.posit.co` serves, byte for byte, verified by SHA-256, so a tab of this gallery looks like a tab of the other Shiny galleries. `_quarto.yml` points at it with the `favicon` key, and the comment beside it records where the image came from.

I did not use the higher-resolution hex from the `shiny` package. That one carries "www.rstudio.com" along its bottom edge, which is stale branding and an unreadable smudge at tab size.

## Verification

`quarto render` emits `<link href="./favicon.png" rel="icon" type="image/png">` in `_site/index.html`, which is the same tag `shiny.posit.co` emits, and copies the 5,903-byte file into `_site/`. The icon reaches the live site at the next publish.

title: Vendor genescout v0.1.5, which fixes the ID-validation seam

title: Publish recount-explorer, and give its tile a screenshot
description:
`recount-explorer` was the last tile on `placeholder.svg`, and the reason was that the application had never been deployed. Its tile carried a comment instead of a `content_id`: the first deployment of an application is the one manual step in this repository, because Connect Cloud creates the id and rsconnect cannot find content by name. #38 then held the whole deploy job back, so nothing was going to make that first deployment either.

## Summary

I deployed it by hand with `.github/scripts/deploy_app.R` under the `posit` account, and the tile now carries the resulting `content_id`. It joins the matrix of `deploy-apps.yml` as soon as the publishing credential is granted publish permission; nothing else about that job changes.

The deployment needed two runs, and CLAUDE.md now says why. New content has no id until it is deployed, so `deploy_app.R` can only PATCH the vanity name *after* the publish — and a content serves its vanity name as it stood at its last publish. So the first run left `posit-recount-explorer.share.connect.posit.cloud` answering `Page Not Found` while the content-id address served the application. The second run landed the name.

The thumbnail is the Browse catalog, captured at 2400x1600 with `R/capture.R` against the deployed application, and the `alt` text now describes that view rather than the tabs the capture does not show.

## Verification

The application is live and starts, by the test in CLAUDE.md rather than a status code:

```bash
curl -s https://posit-recount-explorer.share.connect.posit.cloud/ | head -4
# <base href="_w_...">, not <title>Posit Connect Cloud</title>
```

`Rscript -e 'source("R/check.R")'` passes, and no longer lists a tile awaiting a real screenshot.

title: Publish the gallery site to Connect Cloud, and add the skill that does it
description:
The site that `index.qmd` renders now serves at
<https://posit-shiny-showcase-bioinformatics.share.connect.posit.cloud/>, and that
address is the homepage of this repository. It is live: the page carries its own
title and cards, thumbnails answer 200, and `robots.txt` says `Allow: /`.

## What is here

`.github/scripts/deploy_showcase.R` deploys `_site` as static content, and
`/publish-showcase` is the skill that operates it end to end. The script is separate
from `deploy_app.R` rather than an argument to it: a static site has no manifest, so
rsconnect infers `appMode` and the primary file on its own, and none of the shims
that `deploy_app.R` installs apply. The account, the vanity name and the content id
are constants in the script, because `apps.yml` describes tiles and the page that
shows the tiles is not one of them.

`.github/workflows/deploy-showcase.yml` is the sibling of `deploy-apps.yml` and is
**held back with `if: false`**. The `posit` account has `sso_enabled: true`, and
`PCC_CLIENT_ID` is a client credential that never passes through SSO, so a runner
gets 401 `sso_required`. The comment on that job names both things that must change
together before it can run — deleting the line on its own is not enough, because the
script still asserts the account is already registered. Publish by hand with the
skill meanwhile.

## Two facts recorded in CLAUDE.md

Both cost a while to find, and both look like something else:

- **A rejected write proves nothing unless the body was valid.** Connect Cloud
  validates the body before it checks SSO, so `POST /v1/contents` with an empty body
  answers 422 `request_validation` on a token that cannot write at all. That 422
  reads like "authenticated, bad payload" and is not.
- **The cheap test of a write is a no-op PATCH** of existing content with its own
  `default_robots_policy` and `vanity_name`, reading `errorType` off the condition.
  A PATCH creates no revision, identical values change nothing, and rsconnect
  otherwise prints only `Unauthenticated.`

## renv

`R/renv.lock` gains `rsconnect` **and its dependencies**. `rsconnect` had been
recorded without `httr2`, `openssl`, `packrat`, `snowflakeauth` and five more, so a
fresh clone's `renv::restore()` would have produced a broken install. The scoped
snapshot in the `update-renv` skill now reads `.github/scripts` as well as `R/`;
as written it would have dropped `rsconnect` again on the next update, since nothing
in `R/` names it.

The showcase script therefore runs *under* renv, unlike `deploy_app.R`. That is the
documented difference between the two.

## Verification

- Deployed, then verified the served page, `robots.txt` and a thumbnail over HTTP.
- `Rscript -e 'source("R/check.R")'` passes.
- `python3 .github/scripts/check_secrets.py` passes.
- The final deploy ran under renv on rsconnect 1.11.0.

title: Hold the deploy job back until the publishing credential works
description:
`apps/variant-reviewer` was serving Connect Cloud's spinner page rather than the
application. This holds the deploy job back until the publishing credential
works, and records what the investigation cost.

## What was wrong

The deployed revision still carried the unpatched `.Rprofile`, whose
`is.na(repos["biobouncer"])` is `logical(0)` on Connect Cloud, and
`if (logical(0))` stops R at startup. The patch has been on main since 1fe339b
and never reached Connect Cloud: the deploy run for that commit failed on the
credential, and `deploy-apps.yml` only deploys an application when the push
touched `apps/<app>/` or `apps.yml`, so every push after it reported
`variant-reviewer is unchanged in this push` and stayed green.

**The application is already live again.** It was published by hand, so this
pull request deploys nothing and needs to deploy nothing.

## The deploy job is held back

`deploy_app.R` cannot publish from a runner: the `PCC_CLIENT_ID` and
`PCC_CLIENT_SECRET` secrets hold no publish permission on the account, so every
job stops in `rsconnect::connectCloudClientCredentials()`. Nothing in this
repository can work around that, and a job that fails on every merge teaches
people to ignore a red run.

So the `deploy` job now begins `if: false && ...`, and the comment beside it
carries the reason and the undo. The condition is in the file on purpose:
`gh workflow disable` would put the off switch in GitHub's database instead,
where a reader of this repository cannot see it. The job shows as skipped, not
green, because a green run that deployed nothing is the failure this repository
already warns about.

To deploy again: grant the permission at
<https://login.posit.cloud/identity/credentials>, then delete `false &&`.

## CLAUDE.md

Three facts, each of which cost time here:

- A dead application answers 200 with about 5 kB, close enough to a live one to
  fool a size check. Read the body: a live one carries `<base href="_w_...">`.
- A failed deploy is not retried by the next push, for the reason above.
- A local deploy needs SSO. The account has `sso_enabled: true`, and Connect
  Cloud rejects every write from a token that did not come through it, with a
  bare `401 Unauthenticated` that rsconnect prints without the `sso_required`
  reason in the body. Reads are unaffected, and this content is public, so a
  successful read proves nothing about the token.

`apps.yml` is unchanged.

title: Use the documented account argument, and record why the deploy failed
description:
## Summary

The first real run of `Deploy apps` failed all four jobs at authentication: `Account "posit" is visible to these credentials but does not grant publish permission.`

This started as a work-around for that and ended up reverted, because the message misdescribes its own cause. The name was right, the account was right, and the credential simply holds no publish role. `connectCloudClientCredentials()` registers an account only when `GET /v1/accounts` advertises `content:create` on it, so the remedy is to grant that at <https://login.posit.cloud/identity/credentials>. Nothing in this repository can fix it, and the bypass I had written could only have moved the failure from the registration to the deployment, since it skipped rsconnect's check without establishing whether the API enforces the same one.

So the only code change left is the argument spelling: `accountName = account` becomes `account = account`, matching the [Connect Cloud documentation](https://docs.posit.co/connect-cloud/user/publish/console-or-terminal.html). The two are one call — `account` partial-matches the `accountName` formal — so this is cosmetic, and deliberately so.

The rest is what the investigation cost, written down so it is not paid twice.

`CLAUDE.md` gains fault 5: the failure, the remedy, and the two false leads that looked like the cause and were not. It also gains a **"This repository is public"** section. That one is not incidental: an earlier commit on this branch put a Connect Cloud account id into `CLAUDE.md`, and a diagnostic step printed the id, display name and full permission list of every account the credentials can see into an Actions log, which is world-readable here. Both are removed. The section records the rule and the reason it has to be a rule about the first write: a pull request body keeps every revision through `userContentEdits`, and a force-pushed commit stays fetchable by its SHA, so neither can be un-published without GitHub Support.

`deploy-apps.yml` gains a comment answering a question the gate invites: what happens when packages should move but no application code does. It already works, because every version is pinned in `apps/<app>/manifest.json`, so taking a newer package means rewriting a file under `apps/<app>/`. The comment also records the inverse, which is the part worth remembering: a deployment that leaves the manifest alone changes no package version.

## Verification

- `deploy_app.R` is `main` plus two lines. Ran it with credentials that cannot authenticate, and it fails at the token exchange as expected rather than continuing with no account registered.
- `deploy-apps.yml` loaded back through `yaml::read_yaml()`, confirming the enlarged comment left the `run` script and the five `env` keys intact.
- No Connect Cloud account id remains anywhere in the branch.
- The four gallery applications are unaffected and still serving; this branch changes no deployment behaviour.

**This does not make the deploy work.** After merging, the workflow still fails at authentication until the credential behind `PCC_CLIENT_ID` is granted publish permission on `posit`. Then `gh workflow run deploy-apps.yml` deploys all four.

title: Update the renv library, and record only what R/ reaches
description:
The output of running `/update-renv` (the skill in #36) for the first time. Two commits, because the skill's own advice is to separate a version change from a package removal.

Depends on nothing in #36 — the skill is documentation, this is the lockfile.

## 1. `Update the packages of the renv library`

`renv::update()` moved **28 of the 57** packages. The larger steps: `curl` 7.0.0 → 8.0.0, `fs` 1.6.6 → 2.1.0, `rlang` 1.1.6 → 1.3.0, `vctrs` 0.6.5 → 0.7.3, `zip` 2.3.3 → 3.0.2. `renv::snapshot()` moved the recorded R version 4.5.1 → 4.5.2.

renv itself moved 1.1.5 → 1.2.4, which is why `R/renv/activate.R` is in this commit. That was not a choice — renv is in the lockfile, so `renv::update()` moves it, and moving it rewrites the bootstrap script. Its diff has nothing to review.

## 2. `Record only the packages that R/ reaches, dropping 28`

`snapshot.type` is `implicit`, and the only code this lockfile serves is `R/check.R` and `R/capture.R`. Between them they name seven packages — `chromote`, `fs`, `here`, `jsonlite`, `renv`, `stringr`, `yaml` — which need 29 with their recursive dependencies. The lockfile held 57.

The 28 that go are a tail from an earlier version of the tooling. `googledrive` is the clearest: nothing in the repository names it, and it brought `gargle`, `httr`, `openssl`, `askpass`, `uuid` and `rappdirs`. `readr` brought `vroom`, `tzdb`, `hms`, `clipr`, `bit64`, `bit`, `prettyunits`, `progress`. `dplyr` and `tidyr` brought `tibble`, `pillar`, `purrr`, `tidyselect`, `generics`, `utf8`, `pkgconfig`, `crayon`, `mime`, `sys`.

This commit changes no version, so its diff is removals alone.

## Verification

Both consumers were tested, `R/capture.R` included, because `R/check.R` never touches the chromote and websocket stack:

- `source("R/check.R")` gives 10 tiles in 1 category and 4 supporting packages, the same as before.
- `source("R/capture.R")`, then `open_app()` against a deployed application: the session reported the page title `GeneScout`, and `capture_app()` wrote a 351 KB PNG at 2400x1600. The throwaway PNG was deleted.

**The removal was tested, not reasoned about.** The 29-package lockfile was restored into an empty library outside the project (`RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/tmp/renv-fresh-lib`), which installed exactly 29 packages, and against that library `check.R` and the `capture.R` path both pass. That is what a person cloning this repository and running `renv::restore()` gets.

`check_manifests.py`, `check_secrets.py`, `check_sources.py` and `test_deploy_matrix.py` pass, with the six pre-existing checksum warnings and nothing new.

## One thing to decide

The lockfile points at `packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest` with no snapshot date, so these versions are "whatever CRAN had on 2026-09-04". If you would rather the lockfile were reproducible, the change is a dated P3M URL, and it is not in this PR.

title: Add the update-renv skill
description:
`R/renv.lock` holds the packages that `R/check.R` and `R/capture.R` need. Updating it has one trap, and the trap is silent, so this writes the procedure down.

## The trap

`R/renv/settings.json` sets `snapshot.type` to `implicit`, so renv derives the lockfile from the code it finds in the project — and it finds `apps/`. `renv::dependencies()` discovers 69 packages in this repository, and 62 of them are reached only through `apps/`: `duckdb`, `SummarizedExperiment`, `igvShiny`, `shinyreact`, and several that exist only in a Posit-internal repository. A bare `renv::snapshot()` tries to record all 62 in the gallery's lockfile.

Seven packages come from `R/` — `chromote`, `fs`, `here`, `jsonlite`, `renv`, `stringr`, `yaml` — so the skill snapshots that set and lets renv add the recursive dependencies:

```r
renv::snapshot(packages = unique(renv::dependencies("R", quiet = TRUE)$Package))
```

`renv::status()` reports the same confusion as a long list of packages that are "used" and not "recorded". The skill says those lines are `apps/`, and not a problem to fix.

## The rest of it

- **Test `R/capture.R`, not only `R/check.R`.** An update can break the chromote and websocket stack while every other check passes. The failure would then appear the next time somebody captured a thumbnail, a long way from the commit that caused it. The step opens a deployed application, so it needs no local server.
- **The paths are not the default ones.** `.Rprofile` sets `RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE` to `R/`, so a command that names `renv.lock` writes a second lockfile at the root that nothing reads.
- **`renv::upgrade()` is a separate commit.** It rewrites `R/renv/activate.R`, which is a large diff with nothing to review in it.
- The lockfile carries a tail of packages that no code reaches any more, `googledrive` and its dependencies among them. The scoped snapshot removes them, and that is a different decision from a version update.
- The skill also says, in its description and its first paragraph, that this is **not** `apps/*/manifest.json`. Those are written by `rsconnect::writeManifest()` in each application's own repository, and renv has no part in them.

## Shape

`.agents/skills/update-renv/SKILL.md`, symlinked into `.claude/skills/`, beside `update-thumbnails`. README's file map records both, and the renv section of README now points at the skill.

## Verification

The two claims that carry numbers were measured, not estimated: `renv::dependencies()` gives 69 packages project-wide and 7 from `R/` alone, and nothing in `R/` or `index.qmd` names `googledrive`. `renv::status()` was run to confirm what it reports before a restore.

The `renv::restore()`, `renv::update()` and `renv::snapshot()` steps are **not** exercised end to end here — no library is restored in this worktree, and doing it would install about 60 packages to prove a documented command. The scoped-snapshot call is the one line worth a second reading for that reason.

`check_manifests.py`, `check_secrets.py`, `check_sources.py` and `test_deploy_matrix.py` all pass, with the six pre-existing checksum warnings and nothing new.

title: Patch variant-reviewer .Rprofile so it starts on Connect Cloud
description:
Fixes #30.

`apps/variant-reviewer/.Rprofile` reads `is.na(repos["biobouncer"])`. That is
`logical(0)` when `getOption("repos")` is empty, and `if (logical(0))` is an
error. Connect Cloud starts R with no repos set, so R stopped at startup and
the application served nothing on every deployment.

The guard is now `!("biobouncer" %in% names(repos))`, which holds whether
`repos` is empty, set without the entry, or already has it.

## The vendoring rule, and why this patches it here anyway

`.Rprofile` is vendored, so the fix belongs in `samuelbharti/variant-reviewer`.
That repository is still at v2.3.1 with the `is.na` form, and `main` has no fix,
so waiting means the application stays dead. The patch therefore lives here,
beside a comment in `apps/sources.yml` that tells the reviewer of the next
vendor pull request to read `.Rprofile` of the new release and re-apply this if
the `is.na` form survives. `CLAUDE.md` records the exception.

`manifest.json` carries the checksum of the patched file.

## The tile

`apps.yml` takes back `content_id: 01a06d89-069b-1b9b-e8a7-be4da970cbcf` and
drops `deploy: false`, so `deploy_matrix.py` lists the application again at
`https://posit-variant-reviewer.share.connect.posit.cloud/`.

## Verification

The guard, in R with `options(repos = character())`: the old form errors, the
new one sets the repository. With `repos` already holding `biobouncer`, the new
form leaves the value alone.

`check_manifests.py`, `check_sources.py`, `deploy_matrix.py`,
`test_deploy_matrix.py`, `check_secrets.py` and `R/check.R` all pass.

The deployment itself is not verified here; it needs the Connect Cloud secrets
and runs on merge to main. Read the body size in that job, not only the status
code: a working application here returns tens of kilobytes, and this one
returned 61 bytes while it was broken.

title: Update the README: drop the stale caution, add source and citation
description:
Closes #26

## Summary

**The caution block.** Every claim in it was false. The repository is public (`gh repo view` → PUBLIC), and `gene-list-builder`, named there as private, now has a public repository and a DOI. What remains true is narrower, so the replacement `[!IMPORTANT]` note says only that: the four `lifescience-shiny-gallery` applications carry `deploy: false` until a sanitization pass, and nothing publishes them.

**Source and citation.** A new section, above "Two kinds of content": a table of the five public applications, each with its source repository and its Zenodo DOI, then the citation form and the one distinction that matters. The DOI in `apps.yml` is a *version* DOI; Zenodo also mints a concept DOI, which resolves to the newest version. Cite the version to name the software a piece of work used, the concept to name the application. The four internal applications have neither a public source nor a DOI, and the section says so rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

Nothing here is from memory. The five DOIs each answer 200, and the citation string, the version `0.1.2` and the concept DOI all come from `zenodo.org/api/records/21950641`.

**Three counts that had gone stale beside the code that moved**, found while checking the above against `apps.yml` and `apps/sources.yml`:

- "Three applications have no links" is four. Genome Explorer was added since.
- The vendored list is five, not three: `gene-list-builder` and `plotomics-live` have entries in `sources.yml`. Corrected in `CLAUDE.md` too, which carried the same list.
- The example `links:` block used `zenodo.21352389` for genescout. That is genescout's concept DOI, and the tile carries the version DOI.

## Verification

Read the diff; it is documentation alone. To confirm the facts it now states:

```bash
gh repo view --json visibility                 # PUBLIC
grep -cE '^ +repo:' apps/sources.yml           # 5 vendored applications
grep -c 'deploy: false' apps.yml               # 5: the four internal, plus variant-reviewer
curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21950641
curl -sL https://zenodo.org/api/records/21950641 | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i conceptdoi
```

`apps.yml` and `packages.yml` are untouched, so `R/check.R` and `deploy_matrix.py` see no change.

title: Add recount-explorer to the gallery
description:
Closes #25.

- `apps/sources.yml`: vendor `samuelbharti/recount-explorer` at v0.1.1. The include list is exactly the manifest of the release, minus `.Rprofile` (it only sources `renv/activate.R`).
- `apps/recount-explorer/`: the vendored source, from running `vendor_apps.py`.
- `apps.yml`: a tile, with no `content_id` — the application has no Connect Cloud content yet, so `deploy_matrix.py` reports it as WAIT.

Checks run locally: `R/check.R`, `deploy_matrix.py`, `test_deploy_matrix.py`, `check_manifests.py`, `check_secrets.py`, `check_sources.py` — all pass.

Two follow-ups a person has to do:

1. Deploy once by hand with `deploy_app.R`, then write the content id into `apps.yml`.
2. Replace `thumbnails/placeholder.svg` with a screenshot; `R/check.R` reports the tile as awaiting one.

title: Publish the applications to Connect Cloud on merge to main
description:
## Summary

A merge into `main` now publishes each application in `apps/` to the `posit` account on Posit Connect Cloud, one matrix job per application, and only for the applications the merge touched.

**`apps.yml` is the source of truth.** It already described every application; it now also says which ones deploy and where, through `pcc-account`, `app`, `content_id` and `deploy`. `deploy_matrix.py` turns those tiles into the workflow's matrix, so the workflow holds no application list, no content id and no account name. The "View app" button is derived, not stored — the address of a deployment is `https://<pcc-account>-<app>.share.connect.posit.cloud/`, so `showcase.ejs` builds it and `R/check.R` rejects a hand-written one.

**Deployment is from the committed `manifest.json`.** A runner installs `rsconnect` alone and no dependency of any application. This is not an optimisation: three applications name packages that are not on CRAN, so a runner cannot resolve dependencies at all.

**Five faults in rsconnect 1.11.0 are worked around**, each with a comment naming the version and the condition for removal, and each filed upstream: manifest deployment sends `primary_file: null` (rstudio/rsconnect#1366), `appId` does not work for Connect Cloud (#1367), `applications()` aborts (#1368), `upload = FALSE` fails outright (#1369), and content with no `current_revision` can never be deployed again (#1370). `deploy_app.R` also sets `vanity_name` and `default_robots_policy`, which rsconnect does not expose, before it deploys, so a change to either lands in the same run.

**Two false signals are now closed**, and both cost real time. `deployApp()` returns `FALSE` *invisibly* for a failed publish, so the job would have been green for an application that uploaded and then failed to start; the script now stops. And a 200 from the address is not proof the application runs, because Connect Cloud answers for content that failed to start.

**`deploy_matrix.py` is strict about types.** A quoted `"false"` is a string, and a string is true in Python, so an untyped test would deploy an application that a person deliberately held back (#29). `test_deploy_matrix.py` covers that case and 26 others, and `checks.yml` runs the tests before the program so a broken test cannot leave the job green.

`CLAUDE.md` records the rules and the Connect Cloud knowledge, including when to add a fact and when to delete one.

## What deploys, and what does not

| App | Deploys | Address |
|---|---|---|
| tahoe-explorer | yes | https://posit-tahoe-explorer.share.connect.posit.cloud/ |
| genescout | yes | https://posit-genescout.share.connect.posit.cloud/ |
| Plotomics Live | yes | https://posit-plotomics-live.share.connect.posit.cloud/ |
| gene-list-builder | yes | https://posit-gene-list-builder.share.connect.posit.cloud/ |
| variant-reviewer | **no**, `deploy: false` | Does not start on Connect Cloud; #30 |
| de-explorer, signature-scoring, drug-perturbation, genome-explorer | **no**, `deploy: false` | Awaiting a sanitization pass |

The four deployed applications are verified serving real Shiny UIs (35–190 kB of Shiny and bslib assets), public, and with `robots.txt` set to `Allow: /`.

`variant-reviewer` has never started, from its first deployment: its vendored `.Rprofile` reads `repos["biobouncer"]` and `getOption("repos")` is empty on Connect Cloud, so R fails at startup. `.Rprofile` is vendored from `samuelbharti/variant-reviewer`, so the fix belongs there; the tile is held back and shows no "View app" button rather than linking to an application that cannot run.

## Verification

```
python .github/scripts/deploy_matrix.py       # DEPLOY x4, HOLD x5
python .github/scripts/test_deploy_matrix.py  # 27 cases
Rscript -e 'source("R/check.R")'
```

Set `deploy: "false"` (quoted) on a tile, or delete `pcc-account`, and both programs fail rather than deploying.

The workflow itself has never run: it triggers on a push to `main` and on `workflow_dispatch`, and `workflow_dispatch` needs the file on `main` first. Its first real run is this merge.

title: Vendor the new app releases and refresh the DOIs
description:
Syncs `apps/` to the latest release of all five vendored applications, and points the tiles at the new Zenodo DOIs.

## Why now

The deployed copies were stale in ways that broke Connect Cloud. Each fix had been on the source repo`s `main` for a while but had never been released, so the vendor workflow had nothing newer to copy.

| App | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| variant-reviewer | v2.3.0 | v2.3.1 |
| gene-list-builder | v0.2.0 | v0.2.1 |
| tahoe-explorer | v0.1.1 | v0.1.2 |
| genescout | v0.1.1 | v0.1.2 |
| plotomics-live | v0.1.0 | v0.1.1 |

## What this fixes in the deployed apps

- **`brand.yml` is now named in the manifest** for gene-list-builder and tahoe-explorer. bslib lists it under Suggests, so Connect Cloud never installed it and `bs_theme(brand = TRUE)` failed at startup.
- **No manifest installs from R-universe any more.** variant-reviewer and gene-list-builder recorded `biobouncer`, `biohttp` and `bioclients` with the R-universe URL as their repository, which Connect Cloud cannot read. All now resolve to the public GitHub source at the commit R-universe built, and biobouncer moves 0.1.2 to 0.1.4.
- **plotomics-live installs `htmltools` from CRAN** instead of a personal fork pinned to a May commit.

Verified on this branch: all four brand-using apps name `brand.yml`, zero packages resolve to R-universe, and htmltools is CRAN everywhere.

## apps.yml

The five tiles pinned version DOIs that pointed at the previous releases. Each now points at the DOI Zenodo minted for the new one, and all five were checked live against the Zenodo API.

## Note on the manifest checksum warnings

`check_manifests.py` passes, with warnings that a few files differ from their manifest checksum. This is pre-existing: `main` already reported it for 4 apps, 14 files in variant-reviewer alone. The sync adds a handful more, all of them files touched by the version bump (`R/utils.R`, `DESCRIPTION`, `CITATION.*`, `README.md`), because the manifests were written before those edits. Nothing here is a package or dependency change. Regenerating each manifest as the last step before tagging would clear it, upstream.

title: Give every Bioconductor package a resolvable repository URL
description:
Connect Cloud failed genome-explorer with:

> repository Bioconductor 3.23 cannot be resolved to a URL

## Cause

That string is not a URL, and it appears in the manifest verbatim. Four packages recorded their repository by **name** instead of by address:

```
"Repository": "Bioconductor 3.23"     GenomicRanges, IRanges, Seqinfo, igvShiny
```

Connect resolves a handful of repository names it knows, which is why the 91 CRAN packages recording `"CRAN"` or `"RSPM"` are fine. `Bioconductor 3.23` is not one of them, so resolution stops there and names it in the error.

## Two more problems in the same eight entries

Fixing only the four would have moved the failure rather than ending it.

**Three pointed at r-universe**, the same class of URL that broke the other apps. One of them cannot serve what the manifest pins:

| Package | Pinned | `bioc.r-universe.dev` serves |
|---|---|---|
| BiocVersion | 3.23.1 | **3.24.0** |

That repo tracks Bioconductor devel, so the pinned release version is not there at all.

**GenomeInfoDbData had no `Repository` field**, the only package of 99 in this manifest without one. `rsconnect` reports `Repository must be specified` for a Bioconductor package in that state.

## Fix

All eight now point at the official Bioconductor 3.23 repository, and I verified each URL serves the exact pinned version:

| Package | Pinned | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| igvShiny | 1.8.3 | yes |
| BiocGenerics | 0.58.1 | yes |
| BiocVersion | 3.23.1 | yes |
| GenomicRanges | 1.64.0 | yes |
| IRanges | 2.46.0 | yes |
| S4Vectors | 0.50.1 | yes |
| Seqinfo | 1.2.0 | yes |
| GenomeInfoDbData | 1.2.15 | yes, from the annotation path |

No package version changes. No repository name and no r-universe URL is left in the file. Eight lines, one manifest.

Bioconductor 3.23 pairs with R 4.6, and the previous PR moved this manifest to `platform: 4.6.0`, inside the range Connect Cloud supports, so the pairing is consistent.

title: Record htmltools from CRAN, and pin R to a version Connect Cloud supports
description:
First fix for the deployment failures. It closes the largest single cause and touches nothing on your machine.

## The cause

This machine has `htmltools` **0.5.9.9000** installed from `samuelbharti/htmltools`, a fork of `rstudio/htmltools`. `rsconnect` records where each installed package came from, so six manifests named **GitHub** as the source of htmltools. Connect Cloud then has to fetch it from GitHub instead of CRAN.

The fork is not an accident: `shinyreact` needs it, and only `plotomics-live` uses `shinyreact`. The four applications here do not, so CRAN is the correct source for them.

## Method

I generated the manifests against a **separate library** holding CRAN htmltools 0.5.9, with that library first on `.libPaths()`. Nothing on this machine changed, so your fork stays available for shinyreact.

## Result

Each manifest records exactly one change:

```
htmltools: 0.5.9.9000 (github)  ->  0.5.9 (CRAN)
```

No other package, no other version, no file added or removed, in any of the four.

| App | Non-CRAN packages now |
|---|---|
| de-explorer | **none** |
| drug-perturbation | **none** |
| signature-scoring | **none** |
| genome-explorer | 8 Bioconductor, see below |

Those first three should now deploy.

## A correction to what I told you earlier

I said genome-explorer's Bioconductor entries pointing at `bioc-release.r-universe.dev` looked like a mistake. **They are not.** I reinstalled those packages using `BiocManager::repositories()` and the binaries still came from r-universe, because that is how Bioconductor distributes arm64 macOS binaries. The DESCRIPTION records the URL it was installed from, so the manifest is accurate.

So "Bioconductor 3.23 cannot be resolved" is not about those URLs. Bioconductor 3.23 is the **current release**, published with R 4.6.0, so the likely cause is that Connect Cloud does not offer 3.23 yet. I tried to confirm which Bioconductor snapshots Posit Package Manager serves and my probe used the wrong URL pattern, so I have **not** verified it. I am not going to guess further.

## Still broken, and what each needs

| App | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| genome-explorer | Bioconductor 3.23 | Build against an R version whose Bioconductor release Connect Cloud supports, or drop `igvShiny` |
| plotomics-live | `shinyreact` is in `posit-dev/shinyreact`, **a private repo** | Make it public, or vendor it. Upstream fix |
| gene-list-builder | `biobouncer`, `biohttp`, `bioclients` are R-universe only | Install them from their public GitHub repos before writing the manifest, so Connect can download them. Upstream fix |
| variant-reviewer | `biobouncer` | Same. Upstream fix |
| tahoe-explorer | `ltc` from `loukesio/ltc-color-palettes`, public | Probably installs. Worth one test deploy |

---

## Second commit: the Bioconductor failure, found

The theory above, that Connect Cloud does not offer Bioconductor 3.23, is **wrong**. I said the probe used the wrong URL pattern and had not been verified; it now has been, and the packages are all there.

The correct Posit Package Manager path is `/bioconductor/packages/3.23/bioc/`, not `/bioconductor/3.23/`, which is why the earlier probe 404'd. Every pinned package resolves at exactly the pinned version, from both bioconductor.org and PPM:

| Package | Pinned | bioconductor.org | PPM |
|---|---|---|---|
| igvShiny | 1.8.3 | yes | yes |
| BiocGenerics | 0.58.1 | yes | yes |
| BiocVersion | 3.23.1 | yes | yes |
| GenomicRanges | 1.64.0 | yes | yes |
| IRanges | 2.46.0 | yes | yes |
| S4Vectors | 0.50.1 | yes | yes |
| Seqinfo | 1.2.0 | yes | yes |
| GenomeInfoDbData | 1.2.15 | yes | yes, annotation path |

So availability was never the problem, and dropping `igvShiny` is not necessary.

### The actual cause

**Connect Cloud supports R 4.0.0 through 4.6.0.** Every manifest in this repository pins `"platform": "4.6.1"`, one patch release above the ceiling.

Bioconductor pairs each release with an R minor version, and 3.23 pairs with **R 4.6**. When the requested 4.6.1 is not on offer, the R that does get used no longer matches the Bioconductor release the manifest pins, and the install fails naming 3.23. That matches the error, and it explains why genome-explorer failed on Bioconductor while the other apps failed on ordinary packages: it is the only app here with any Bioconductor dependency.

### The fix

`"platform"` becomes `"4.6.0"` in all four manifests. That is inside the supported range, and it is still R 4.6, so Bioconductor 3.23 remains the correct pairing and no package version has to move.

It also matches how the packages were actually built. Counting the `Built:` strings, 96 of 99 packages in genome-explorer were built under R 4.6.0, and only 3 under 4.6.1. The same holds for the other three apps.

One line changed per manifest, four lines in total. `check_manifests.py` still passes.

### Not fixed here

The five vendored apps also pin 4.6.1, and their manifests come from upstream releases, so this repository cannot correct them. That needs `rsconnect::writeManifest()` re-run under R 4.6.0 upstream, followed by a new release of each.

title: Name brand.yml in the manifest of de-explorer
description:
Fixes the deployment error you hit: **"The package `brand.yml` is required"**.

## Why it happened

`apps/de-explorer/app.R` calls:

```r
theme = bslib::bs_theme(brand = "_brand.yml", primary = "#447099")
```

bslib reads `_brand.yml` through a package literally named **`brand.yml`**, and bslib only **suggests** it:

```
Suggests: brand.yml, bsicons, curl, fontawesome, future, ggplot2, ...
```

Nothing in the app code says `library(brand.yml)` or `brand.yml::`, so `rsconnect::writeManifest()` never saw the dependency and left it out of `manifest.json`. Connect Cloud installs exactly what the manifest names, so the package was missing at run time.

## Why only some apps break

The two bslib code paths behave completely differently:

| Call | Function | Behaviour when `brand.yml` is absent |
|---|---|---|
| `bs_theme()` | `brand_resolve.NULL` | `is_installed("brand.yml")`, returns `NULL`. **Starts, silently unbranded** |
| `bs_theme(brand = "_brand.yml")` | `brand_resolve.character` | `rlang::check_installed("brand.yml")`. **Stops** |

So passing the path is what turns a missing suggested package into a hard failure.

## Every app, checked

| App | Passes `brand =` | `brand.yml` in manifest | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| de-explorer | yes | **no** | **broken**, fixed here |
| tahoe-explorer | yes | **no** | **broken**, needs an upstream fix |
| gene-list-builder | yes | **no** | **broken**, needs an upstream fix |
| genescout | yes | yes | fine |
| variant-reviewer | yes | yes | fine |
| drug-perturbation, genome-explorer, signature-scoring | no | no | unaffected, see below |
| plotomics-live | no `_brand.yml` | n/a | unaffected |

genescout and variant-reviewer are fine because their manifests come from `renv.lock`, which records `brand.yml` as a project dependency. The others are scanned from code, which is where the gap appears.

## The fix

`app.R` gains one call, with a comment explaining why it is there:

```r
requireNamespace("brand.yml", quietly = TRUE)
```

rsconnect now finds the dependency. The regenerated manifest **adds exactly one package**, `brand.yml` 0.1.0 from CRAN. No other package changed, no version changed, no file added or removed.

I confirmed the app still starts and still themes: the compiled Bootstrap CSS contains `#447099`, `#419599` and `#72994E` from `_brand.yml`.

## A `.posit` leak this nearly caused

The first regenerated manifest named two files under `.posit/publish/`, which hold the Connect Cloud `server_url`, the content GUID and the dashboard URL. rsconnect does not ignore that directory, and `.gitignore` does not help here, because rsconnect reads the working directory.

So all four local applications gain a `.rscignore`:

```
.posit
.Renviron
.Renviron.example
```

The three that are not affected by the brand bug get it as prevention. Their manifests are unchanged. This is the same class of fix as genescout#34, and it is what #18 could not cover on its own.

## Three things not fixed here

**`tahoe-explorer` and `gene-list-builder` will fail the same way.** They are vendored, so the fix belongs upstream, one call plus a regenerated manifest and a release, exactly as here.

**`drug-perturbation`, `genome-explorer` and `signature-scoring` never call `bs_theme()`.** They build their UI with `tagList()` and their own CSS, so their `_brand.yml` files are unused. Not a bug, but those four files are dead weight.

**I did not regenerate the other three manifests.** Doing so pulled in unrelated drift: my local BiocManager comes from RSPM rather than CRAN, which rewrote provenance fields in `genome-explorer`. I reverted it and left those manifests alone.

title: Ignore .posit at every level, and refuse it in a test
description:
Posit Publisher writes `.posit` next to an application. Its files record the **server URL, the content GUID, the dashboard URL and the log URL** of a deployment. None of that should be published.

## It was already here

`apps/de-explorer/.posit` exists in the working tree right now, with a Connect Cloud `server_url` and an `id` GUID in `deployment-K80K.toml`. git had not recorded it, so nothing leaked, but nothing was stopping the next `git add -A` either.

## Three layers

**1. `.gitignore`** gets `.posit/` with no leading slash, so it applies at every level. Verified by creating the directory at three depths:

```
.gitignore:15:.posit/   .posit/publish/a.toml
.gitignore:15:.posit/   apps/genescout/.posit/publish/b.toml
.gitignore:15:.posit/   apps/genescout/R/.posit/c.toml
.gitignore:15:.posit/   apps/de-explorer/.posit/publish/de-explorer-H6DG.toml
```

**2. `check_secrets.py`** gets a second test. The existing one reads the *name* of each file, and a name like `deployment-K80K.toml` gives no sign of the problem, so the new test reads each part of the path. A force-added `.posit` now fails CI:

```
ERROR    apps/demo/.posit/publish/demo-H6DG.toml
ERROR    apps/demo/.posit/publish/deployments/deployment-K80K.toml
2 file(s) must not be in this repository.   exit=1
```

**3. `check_sources.py`** refuses an `include` list that names `.posit`, so the vendor bot cannot copy one in from a source repository. That path already existed for `.Renviron` and keys, and `.posit` joins the list.

Ignoring alone would have been enough for today. The other two matter because `apps/` receives files from five repositories I do not control.

## One thing beyond the ask

`.DS_Store` was also untracked and unignored, three of them. I added it. That is the exact failure mode that nearly committed six `.rds` cache files in #16, so it seemed worth closing while I was in the file.

## Not done here

`samuelbharti/genescout` has an untracked `.posit/` too, and its `.gitignore` does not cover it. Its `.rscignore` already keeps it out of deployment bundles, which I fixed in genescout#34, but git there would still take it. Same for any other app repo you have published from. Say the word and I will do the same one-line fix across them.

title: Give every tile a real image

`samuelbharti/plotomics` has `assets/logo.svg`, a proper hex at `viewBox="0 0 174 200"`, matching `biohttp.svg` and `bioclients.svg` at `0 0 173.2 200`. The tile now uses it with `fit: hex`, like the other three package tiles.

## tahoe-explorer and gene-list-builder get screenshots

**tahoe-explorer**: the Tahoe-100M overview. Header, the six count cards (100.6M cells, 50 cell lines, 379 drugs), the cell-lines-by-organ chart and the driver-gene table. Reads well in the 3:2 crop.

description:
## The rename

| Local | `de-explorer`, `signature-scoring`, `drug-perturbation`, `genome-explorer` | Here |

With the matching warning: do not edit a vendored app here, the next run overwrites it.

One thing this did not test: `source("R/check.R")` fails on this machine with `there is no package called 'here'`. That is the project renv library being incomplete locally, not a change from this PR. It needs `renv::restore()`. Nothing in `R/` or `renv.lock` was touched.

title: Add manifest, sources.yml and secret tests on each pull request
description:
Everything I have been testing by hand for the last three PRs, as three jobs in `.github/workflows/checks.yml`.

They operate on every pull request and on `main` after a merge. No path filter: a test that does not operate gives a false result, and these take seconds.

## The three jobs

**Manifests** (`check_manifests.py`). Compares each directory in `app/` with its own `manifest.json`. Errors on a file the manifest names and the directory does not contain, and on a package the code loads that the manifest does not name. Warns on a stale checksum, because that means only that the manifest is older than the file.

**sources.yml** (`check_sources.py`). Tests the shape of each entry, then reads each source repository through the API and asks whether `include` copies every file of the manifest. This finds the problem in the pull request that writes the entry, and not later when the vendor workflow operates.

**Secrets** (`check_secrets.py` and gitleaks). gitleaks reads content and finds a value with the shape of a key. `check_secrets.py` reads names, and finds a file such as `.Renviron`, whose content is only `NAME=value` and has no shape to recognize. That risk is real here: the vendor workflow copies from other repositories, and one of them holds a live API key in its root `.Renviron`. `check_sources.py` also refuses an `include` list that names such a file, so it stops before the copy.

The gitleaks Action needs a license for an organization, so the workflow reads the release binary directly. gitleaks itself is free.

## The genescout waiver

genescout fails the manifest test with 141 missing files, for the reason in #6: its manifest describes the whole repository. Adding these tests with no answer for that would leave `main` red.

`allow_missing_manifest_files: true` on the entry turns the error into a warning. The comment above it names the correction (put the paths in `.rscignore`, write the manifest again, publish a release) and states that Connect Cloud cannot deploy genescout until then. So the problem stays visible and stays described, and no other pull request is blocked by it.

## Testing

Every path was made to fire, not only the passing one:

- All seven applications, real and vendored: only genescout errors, and the waiver turns it into a warning.
- Synthetic applications with an absent `manifest.json`, broken JSON, a missing file, a wrong checksum, and an undeclared package: 3 errors, exit 1.
- A deliberately broken `sources.yml` with a bad name, a bad repo form, a numeric `ref`, an absolute path, a `..` path, a repeated path, no `manifest.json`, a repeated name, a repeated repository, an empty `include` and an unknown key: **12 errors**, and the network phase correctly did not operate.
- An `include` list naming `.Renviron` and `certs/server.key`: both refused, `.Renviron.example` correctly permitted.
- `check_secrets.py` against a scratch repository holding `.Renviron` and `server.key`: both found, the `.example` file permitted.
- gitleaks locally on the working tree, on all 19 commits of history, and on the three vendored candidates: **no leaks**.

Two false positives showed up while I was building this, and both are fixed. `library (recommended):` inside a generated-code string was read as a package, so the necessary-package test now reads only text with the strings and comments removed. And `biogate`, a guarded optional dependency of genescout, was reported as undeclared, so a name inside `requireNamespace()` now counts as optional.

I also confirmed the vendor bot still round-trips `sources.yml` with the new key and its comment: the rewrite is still a clean two-line diff.

## Merge order

This branch is off `main`, and #6 and #7 also edit `app/sources.yml`. Merge those two first. If the waiver then conflicts, it is a three-line resolution.

title: Add variant-reviewer to the vendor list

The manifest also names `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `CITATION.cff` and `CITATION.md`. A deployment does not need them, but Connect Cloud reads every file the manifest names, so they are in the list. This app has a real `.rscignore`, so its manifest describes the application and not the whole repository. `tests/`, `dev/` and `docs/` stay out.

| App | Files in manifest | Missing | Stale checksums |
|---|---|---|---|
| variant-reviewer | 68 | **0** | 14 |
| tahoe-explorer | 61 | 0 | 0 |
| genescout | 231 | 141 | 1 |

## The 14 stale checksums

The manifest was written before the last edits to those files, and it was not written again before the tag. The affected files are `.Rprofile`, `demo_cache.rds`, three modules, seven files under `R/`, and the two CITATION files.

I checked the risk this actually carries: every package that the code loads is already declared in the manifest, so nothing is missing at install time. Regenerating the manifest before the next release corrects this.

I am not certain whether Connect Cloud validates these checksums for a git-backed deploy. If it does, the deploy stops. That is worth one test deploy before you rely on it.

## README correction

|---|---|---|
| tahoe-explorer | 61 | **0** |
| genescout | 231 | 141 |

The change to `app/sources.yml` is two lines, so ruamel kept every comment in the file.

## genescout cannot deploy yet

title: Rewrite the documentation in Simplified Technical English
description:
Applies the ASD-STE100 rules to the documentation of this repository: short sentences, active voice, one word for one meaning, a condition before its command, and no contractions. The aim is text that a reader who is not a native English speaker can understand at the first reading.

## Rewritten

`README.md`, the `update-thumbnails` skill, the comments in `app/sources.yml`, `apps.yml`, `packages.yml` and the workflow, and the comments, docstrings and messages in `R/check.R`, `R/capture.R`, `R/thumbnail-name.R` and `vendor_apps.py`.

## Not rewritten, deliberately

- **The showcase text.** The tile descriptions in `apps.yml` and `packages.yml`, the text of `index.qmd`, and the site description in `_variables.yml`. STE removes persuasion by design, so it is the wrong tool for the cards that present the applications.
- **The source code in `app/`.** The upstream repositories own those comments. The next copy operation would replace anything changed here.

## Three statements corrected

The README said that no remote was configured, that nothing leaves this machine, and that the issue URL was a guess. A remote now exists, three pull requests are merged, and that URL is correct. The README also had no text about `app/` or the vendor workflow, and it now documents both.

`app/sources.yml` regains the note about the four lifescience applications, which PR #2 removed to avoid a merge conflict. The wording now matches the behaviour after PR #3: one application with no release does not stop the other applications.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All three R files parse | OK |
| `check.R` output | 8 tiles, 4 packages, unchanged |
| Every YAML file parses | OK |
| Each rewritten error and warning | Made to fire; each reads correctly |
| Vendor script | Still copies genescout, still keeps the comments of `sources.yml` |
| Workflow YAML | Valid, one trigger, six steps |
| Banned modals, contractions, British spellings, Latin abbreviations | None |
| Sentence limits | Every prose sentence is inside the 20/25 word limits |

title: Port the four lifescience apps into app/, deploy-ready
description:
Copies **DE Explorer**, **Signature Scoring**, **Drug Perturbation** and **Genome Explorer** out of `posit-dev/lifescience-shiny-gallery` into `app/<name>/`. Each is fully self-contained: its own modules, its own data, its own `_brand.yml`, its own `manifest.json`. Nothing was removed from the source repo.

| App | Size | Modules | Boots standalone |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app/de-explorer` | 15 MB | 12 | 200, "DE Explorer" |
| `app/signature-scoring` | 12 MB | 10 | 200, "Signature Scoring" |
| `app/drug-perturbation` | 2.4 MB | 10 | 200, "Drug Perturbation" |
| `app/genome-explorer` | 452 KB | 2 | 200, "Genome Explorer" |

Genome Explorer is the classic Shiny R variant (`apps/genome-explorer/shiny/r`); the Python and shinyreact variants were not ported.

## Why this is a hand-copy, not a bot vendor

The existing vendor bot cannot do this job, and adding these apps to `sources.yml`'s `apps:` list would actively break it. Recorded in full in `app/sources.yml`; briefly:

1. `lifescience-shiny-gallery` has **no tags or releases**, so there is nothing to pin to.
2. Even with a release, a tarball would omit each app's `R/_shared`, `R/_modules` and `_brand.yml`, which are **git-ignored build output** there (produced by that repo's `scripts/sync-shared.R`). The bot would vendor four apps that fail on startup.
3. `vendor_one()` raises on a release-less repo and `main()` has no per-app error isolation, so one such entry **aborts the whole run, genescout included**.

## Structure decision

Kept `R/_shared` and `R/_modules` as subdirectories rather than flattening into `R/`. The leading underscore is load-bearing: Shiny auto-sources top-level `R/*.R`, so flattening would double-source every file on top of the explicit loops each `app.R` already runs. Verified no basename collisions and no top-level calls in those files, so this preserves working behaviour rather than compromising.

## Edits made

Limited to what actually went stale on the move:

- Dropped each app's `_components` file, the sync manifest describing a build step that cannot run here.
- Rewrote the `app.R` header comments that instructed the reader to *"Re-sync with `scripts/sync-shared.R` before running or deploying"*, against a script this repo does not contain.

## Manifests

Generated per app with `rsconnect::writeManifest()`, **pinning R 4.6.1** (worth confirming that matches what Connect Cloud offers).

One thing worth knowing: Genome Explorer's `igvShiny` is **Bioconductor, not CRAN**. Its manifest records `https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.23/bioc`. A manifest naming a Bioconductor package with only CRAN in `repos` installs fine locally and then fails on Connect at install time, so the repo list was set from `BiocManager::repositories()` before writing.

## Verification

- All four **boot standalone** via `shiny::runApp()` on their own directory, serving HTTP 200 with their real titles (not error pages).
- Every package each app loads appears in its manifest; `appmode: shiny` on all four.
- No vendored file is caught by `.gitignore`; no `.Renviron` or secret was copied (the source repo's root `.Renviron` holds a live API key and sits above the copied leaves).
- `quarto render` still emits only `index.html`, confirming the existing `!app/**` exclusion covers the new subdirectories and the four per-app `_brand.yml` files do not disturb the site's brand resolution.
- `R/check.R` clean; `apps.yml`, `packages.yml` and `thumbnails/` untouched, per your "code only" call.

Adds 29 MB, almost entirely bundled CSV (`signature-scoring/data/expression.csv` is 11.5 MB of it).

## Not in this PR

The stuck `vendor-apps-bot` branch: 4 failed runs, still blocked by "GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests". Genescout's vendored files are sitting on that branch with no PR attached.

title: Make vendoring a manual two-command flow
description:
The `posit-dev` org forbids GitHub Actions from creating pull requests, and the setting is greyed out at repo level, so only an org owner can lift it. Four scheduled runs have now failed on that one API call, each after successfully vendoring and pushing the branch.

Rather than wait on org approval or introduce a credential to work around it, the workflow now stops at pushing the branch and leaves the PR to a human.

## The flow

```bash
gh workflow run vendor-apps.yml -R posit-dev/shiny-showcase-bioinformatics   # vendor + push branch
gh pr create --head vendor-apps-bot --fill                                    # open the PR
```

One run still covers **every** app, so it's two commands per release batch, not per app. The job summary prints the exact `gh pr create` line.

No token, no secret, no workflow in the app repos, nothing that expires or needs org approval.

## Also drops the daily cron

GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days without repository activity, and a gallery updated a few times a year would trip that. A `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow is never disabled. The unused `pull-requests` permission goes too.

## Two robustness fixes, both needed before the other app repos can be listed

- An app with **no Release** is reported as `WAIT` and skipped rather than raising, so it can sit in `sources.yml` before its first release and start syncing by itself once one appears.
- Each app is **isolated** in its own `try/except`. One failing entry no longer stops the others, and the run still exits non-zero so the failure stays visible.

Testing the first of those turned up a bug in it: `/releases/latest` returns 404 both for *"no releases yet"* and for *"no such repo"*, so a typo'd repo name reported as `WAIT` and would have looked healthy forever. It now probes the repo itself to tell the two apart, and a missing or inaccessible repo is a hard error naming the likely cause.

## Verified against the live API

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| genescout, already pinned | `SKIP` |
| genescout, unpinned | `BUMPED (none) -> v0.1.0` |
| variant-reviewer, real repo with no release | `WAIT` |
| nonexistent repo | `ERROR`, exit 1 |
| bad include path | `ERROR`, other apps still vendored, exit 1 |
| `sources.yml` round-trip | only the `ref` line changes, comments intact |

## Status of the remaining app repos

Recorded in `sources.yml` rather than added blind, since none is ready:

| Repo | Release | `manifest.json` |
|---|---|---|
| `tahoe-explorer` | v0.1.0 | **missing** |
| `variant-reviewer` | **none** | yes |
| `gene-list-builder` | **none** | **missing** |

Only genescout is currently both released and deploy-ready, so it stays the only entry.

## Note

This branches off `main`, and PR #2 also edits `app/sources.yml`. The two touch different regions so they should auto-merge, but whichever lands second may want a glance.

title: Add app/ vendoring scaffold and bot
description:
Adds the mechanism to pull real app source into `app/<name>/` for direct Connect deployment from this repo, prototyped on genescout. Deployment itself is out of scope here, this only prepares `app/` to hold real, deployable source.

## What's here

- **`app/sources.yml`** — config: per app, a source repo, a pinned release tag, and an explicit include-list of paths to vendor. Deliberately an allowlist, not "the whole release tarball": genescout's repo carries tests, an eval harness, `CLAUDE.md` and other dev-only files that have no place in a deployed artifact. `manifest.json` is always included; it's produced by the source repo, not generated here.
- **`.github/scripts/vendor_apps.py`** — checks a repo's latest GitHub Release, and where that's ahead of the pinned `ref`, downloads that release's tarball and copies the include-list into `app/<name>/`. Uses ruamel.yaml's round-trip mode so the comments in `sources.yml` survive being rewritten by a bot.
- **`.github/workflows/vendor-apps.yml`** — runs that script on a schedule or manual dispatch, opens a PR only when a real `git diff` shows something changed.
- **`_quarto.yml`** — excludes `app/` from this site's own render (genescout ships its own `report/template.qmd`, which would otherwise get built as a page here).

## Tested locally before pushing

Ran the script by hand: vendored genescout cleanly (1.1MB, exactly the include-list, no stray tests/dev/evals), the `sources.yml` diff was just the one `ref` line, `quarto render` still produced only `index.html` with `app/` present. Then reset `app/` back to unvendored so the workflow does the first vendor itself, once this merges, rather than this PR doing it by hand.

## Note

GitHub only allows dispatching a `workflow_dispatch` workflow once its file exists on the default branch, so triggering this for real has to wait until this PR is merged.
